subject: Access controls & data handling - follow-up from demo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Access controls & data handling - follow-up from demo

Hi Sam -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the next steps we committed to on the call around data handling and access controls. Please correct me if I missed anything.

Summary of what we covered
- PII: FinTrust will send examples of sensitive fields (SSNs, account numbers) so we can confirm transformation/PII masking guidance. Redwood does not use customer prompt/content for model training unless explicitly opted-in.
- Data residency: you flagged that certain data needs to remain in the EU for regulatory reasons (we discussed options).
- Retention & logging: retention configurable per-customer; audit logs capture admin/support actions and API calls.
- RBAC & least privilege: role-based model (owner/admin/developer/read-only) with resource-level scoping and optional integration with customer's IdP via SCIM/SCIM groups.
- Support access / break-glass: short-lived elevation flow with MFA and mandatory ticket reference; all elevation events produce an immutable audit trail.

Attachments I attached to this email: redwood_rbac_whitepaper.pdf, SOC2-TypeII-Attestation.pdf.

Next steps
1) Sam to confirm whether FinTrust needs EU-only residency for production inference (yes/no + which datasets).
2) We will share the break-glass playbook and a short tech note on how support access is audited (attached).
3) Schedule a 30-min architecture follow-up with Michael and Dev to walk through RBAC mappings and integration work (CC'd).
4) Provide any specific compliance evidence FinTrust needs for procurement (e.g., specific logging retention windows).

If that looks right, I'll send the playbook and propose times for the follow-up.

Best,
Marissa
Head of Solutions - Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

---
Redwood Inference | Making inference predictable and economical

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@fintrust.com>

Subject: Re: Access controls & data handling - follow-up from demo

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful. A few clarifications from my side:

- Residency: For customer-identifiable financial datasets we require EU-only residency for production (not just backups). Non-sensitive metadata can remain in the US.
- PII: We'll share a sample schema tomorrow. We also need to know whether Redwood supports tokenization or redaction at ingestion (we prefer tokenization).
- Support access: Two follow-ups here - 1) can support elevation be limited to encrypted ephemeral keys (we need proof keys aren't stored), and 2) will Redwood tie every elevation to a Jira/ServiceNow ticket and exportable audit log?
- Retention: We maintain data for up to 7 years for some records; can retention policies be set per data-class and exported for evidence?

Finally, what is the expected impact on pricing if we require EU-only residency for inference for a portion of our traffic? Does Redwood have region-specific pricing or capacity fees?

Happy to take the architecture follow-up - I'll propose times after you send proposed slots.

Regards,
Sam Jenkins
Head of Platform Security - FinTrust
sam.jenkins@fintrust.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@fintrust.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access controls & data handling - follow-up from demo

Great questions - answering inline and adding Nikhil (privacy/controls) + Dev (infra) to help with specifics.

- Residency: Yes - we can route inference traffic to a dedicated EU-only cluster for production. That cluster's storage and KV caches can be configured to remain in-region. We'll add a short note on isolation guarantees in the playbook.
- Tokenization/redaction: We support both approaches. Tokenization at ingestion is supported via our ingestion hooks; redaction pipelines can also be applied. We will provide example configs.
- Support elevation: Support-only ephemeral keys are used for break-glass. Keys are generated by the customer's control plane; Redwood does not persist plaintext keys. Every elevation requires MFA and a ticket reference.
- Exportable evidence: Audit logs (who, when, reason, scope) are exportable and immutable; we can provide a sample CSV/JSON export. Retention windows are configurable per data-class and we can support long-term retention for legal needs.

I'll attach the break-glass playbook and the RBAC whitepaper to this thread and propose 3 time slots for a 30-min follow-up (Mon/Tue next week).

Action: Nikhil/Dev, can you add a brief note (one paragraph each) about the technical guarantees for EU cluster isolation and how short-lived elevation tokens are issued and logged?

Thanks -
Marissa

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access controls & data handling - follow-up from demo

Sam - adding a few technical details you can share with your security team. Short summary first, details after.

Summary
- RBAC: Role hierarchy (Owner > Admin > Developer > Auditor). Roles map to scoped resource ARNs. Support role is read-only by default and requires break-glass elevation for write-level ops.
- Break-glass: Implemented as a short-lived elevation token flow (15-60 min TTL). Elevation requires: ticket ID, approver (if configured), and MFA. The elevation issuance is recorded in the customer audit log and gateway traces.
- IdP sync: We support SCIM group sync and SCIM mappings to role templates. For customers using OIDC/SCIM, tokens are short-lived (min 5m) and refreshed via the standard provider.
- Encryption & keys: All secrets are stored encrypted at rest using customer KMS when requested. Ephemeral keys used for break-glass are HSM-backed where customers opt-in. Redwood does not persist plaintext tokens.
- Logging & retention: API, admin, and support actions are logged to an append-only stream. Retention windows are configurable per-customer; exports support daily/weekly snapshots for compliance.

Attachments: break-glass-playbook.md (attached)
Links: https://app.redwood.ai/docs/rbac#break-glass (public doc)

If you want, Dev and I can prepare a short architecture diagram showing EU-only cluster routing and the token flow for the follow-up meeting.

- Michael
